title: `load_from_checkpoint` should not be called as an instance method
body:
### Outline & Motivation

Spent a while debugging : 
```python
model.load_from_checkpoint(model_path)
```
which should be : 
```python
model = LitModel.load_from_checkpoint(model_path)
```
there should be a warning when the instance method is called. 

### Pitch

```python
model.load_from_checkpoint(model_path)
```
which should be : 
```python
model = LitModel.load_from_checkpoint(model_path)
```
there should be a warning when the first approach i.e. instance method is called. 

### Additional context

_No response_

cc @participant3 @participant1 @participant4 @participant6

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Thanks for the suggestion @reporter 
We already have an error message for this, but I think we could improve it to give some instructions what to do instead:
https://github.com/Lightning-AI/lightning/blob/df4ad1932b0ad9a5ffe9b335726e4d12f6820f23/src/lightning/pytorch/core/saving.py#L99

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I see. Mistake from my side was assuming behaviour similar to Pytorch's `load_state_dict` which does inplace. If I do :
```python
model = model.load_from_checkpoint(model_path)
```
it works fine. I can open a PR if you suggest the improved instructions. I am familiar with the codebase. I think logging to not call inplace would be nice.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter You are very welcome to open a PR. My suggestion would be to edit this error message here

https://github.com/Lightning-AI/lightning/blob/df4ad1932b0ad9a5ffe9b335726e4d12f6820f23/src/lightning/pytorch/core/saving.py#L99

to this:

```py
if isinstance(cls, LightningModule):
    raise ValueError(
        f"Calling `.load_from_checkpoint` on a model instance is not supported. Please change it to `{type(cls).__name__}.load_from_checkpoint(...)"
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> @reporter You are very welcome to open a PR. My suggestion would be to edit this error message here
> 
> https://github.com/Lightning-AI/lightning/blob/df4ad1932b0ad9a5ffe9b335726e4d12f6820f23/src/lightning/pytorch/core/saving.py#L99
> 
> to this:
> 
> ```python
> if isinstance(cls, LightningModule):
>     raise ValueError(
>         f"Calling `.load_from_checkpoint` on a model instance is not supported. Please change it to `{type(cls).__name__}.load_from_checkpoint(...)"
> ```

This method doesn't actually work, since `_load_from_checkpoint` is called inside the `classmethod` `load_from_checkpoint`, and the first argument (`cls`) is guaranteed to be the subbclass type and not the instance.

comments.author: participant2
participant1
comments.body:
@participant2 This was an oversight on my part. You are right the suggestion I made won't work and now it also becomes clear to me why we haven't done this already in years 😅 

> However, this limits the usage of the classmethod

Could you explain the cons of the `restricted_classmethod` vs. Python's?

Given that this UX question came up several times already in the past, we should definitely consider replacing `classmethod` with such a restricted decorator.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
If we raise an exception, the only con I can think of would be that it precludes this (rare) use case: 

```python
model2 = model.load_checkpoint(...)
```

To prevent breaking changes, we should probably emit a warning instead of raising an exception:

```python
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class restricted_classmethod:
    def __init__(self, method):
        self.method = method
    def __get__(self, instance, cls):
        if instance is not None:
            # Replace with the appropriate logger
            log.warning(f"classmethod {cls.__name__}.{self.method.__name__} called on an instance.")
        return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.method(cls, *args, **kwargs)

```

If we want to implement `restricted_classmethod`, let's first compile a list of classmethods in the lightning code base that would benefit from this.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Adding my 2 cents here: I think the restricted_classmethod is great but it's an unnecessary abstraction. In this case I'd rather have an explicit type check followed by an eventual error in combination with a regular class method -- even at the cost of potential code duplication.

I think this construct would just hurt readability and debugging.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> In this case I'd rather have an explicit type check followed by an eventual error in combination with a regular class method

How would it look like? As pointed out earlier, the check can't be done in the `load_from_checkpoint` function directly as we never get access to the instance. If there is an easier way of doing it without introducing a context manager, I would also prefer that.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant3 I'd like to see your proposal. The reason I proposed the above is because in a `classmethod`, you don't have access to the instance even if the method is called on an instance. `classmethod`s and instance methods live in the same namespace, where the classmethod explicitly ignores the instance even if its present. The only way to have a method recognize whether its called on the type or an instance is by [implementing descriptors](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#implementing-descriptors), as I proposed above.
